precepts.why:
Paul calls it “the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints.” The whole question is who those saints are, and the Psalm answers it: “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” The saints are the children of Israel.

A lot of times, when you pull up these key words, it shuts Christians down. They read “saints” and picture everybody who ever went to church. But the scripture defines its own words. The saints are his people, the children of Israel, and the mystery Paul was made a minister of was made manifest to them.

So when Colossians 1:26 says the mystery is now made manifest “to his saints”, it is saying it is made manifest to Israel. That is who Paul was writing to, and that is who the mystery belongs to.

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” The children of Israel are the saints.

Now read Psalms 50 again with that. “He shall call to the heavens from above”: that is the angels he is calling to. “and to the earth”: the earth is you and I. And the message to both is the same, “Gather my saints together unto me.” That is what we read in Matthew 24, where Christ tells his angels to gather the elect, and it is the commandment to the prophets on earth too.

“those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice”: only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice. So we are not supposed to be looking for other races and other nationalities. The work of gathering is for the twelve tribes of Israel, the saints, scattered to the four corners of the earth.
